To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) if the review information can be sufficiently informative, the seller's best strategy is to adjust its own marketing strategy (e.g., the amount of its product attribute information) in response to consumer review information; (2) the seller's optimal strategy is to provide more product attribute information if the product is relatively inexpensive and/or there are more expert (more sophisticated, more knowledgeable) product users in the market; (3) the seller's profit can be increased by adopting a proactive marketing strategy

(1) when the review information is sufficient, it will be used by consumers to reduce their search effort, and the seller should increase the amount of information provided via marketing communications to compensate for the reduced consumer search effort; (2) the seller can increase the amount of marketing communications to compensate consumers for the reduced search effort, even before reviews are available; (3) when the review is sufficient, the seller should facilitate the review process by allowing consumers to create reviews on the seller’s website,

(1) the seller should adjust the amount of product information it offers to complement the buyer-created review information; (2) when the product cost and number of expert users are high, the seller should reduce the amount of its product information; and (3) the seller can increase profit by introducing the reviews at the right time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how a seller should respond strategically to consumer reviews, and when it is beneficial to facilitate such user-based information.
how the seller should respond to the emergence of consumer product review, and how it should strategically use this information as an additional marketing communications tool to enhance its profit.
the impact of the availability of consumer product reviews on sellers' marketing communications strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
consumer reviews can serve as a valuable source of information for consumers, and the availability of consumer-based information can help the seller to increase its profit.
the seller should adjust the marketing communication strategy in order to maximize profit by considering the product/market conditions and the availability of consumer review information.

consumer reviews are a new type of marketing communication that can serve as a complement or substitute for the traditional seller-created information, and the strategic role of such a new type of information can be quite different depending on the market and product conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

consumer reviews can serve as a powerful marketing communication tool for sellers to increase sales and profit, but only if the seller adjusts its marketing communication strategy appropriately in response to the availability of consumer-generated information.
consumer product reviews can serve as a powerful marketing communication tool and that the seller should strategically manage this tool to enhance its profit.
consumer reviews, as a new element of marketing communication mix, can help the seller improve its profit by adjusting its own marketing communication strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the seller can increase profit by adjusting its marketing communication strategy in the presence of online consumer product reviews and by facilitating the provision of consumer reviews.
consumer reviews can be a powerful marketing tool that can be used to complement or substitute for the traditional marketing communication strategies.
online consumer review can be viewed as a new element of the marketing communication mix.
